newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Dec 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Dec 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Saturday urged the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) to end their parliament boycott to discuss all national issues including the Ganges water sharing treaty with India.
Police in Rangamati hill district arrested a youngman on Saturday in connection with the assassination of pro-peace tribal leader Subinoy Chakma.
At least 15 labourers were killed and 25 others injured when the truck carrying them rolled into a roadside ditch on Dhaka-Maymensingh highway on Saturday.
Some 9,036 Bangladeshis are expected to perform hajj in 1997 under government arrangement.
Traders in the kerb market start on Sunday sit-in demonstration for indefinite period in front of the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) building to protest continuing slide in share prices.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said the state-run media would not work as the publicity organs of the the ruling party.
Some 38 companies listed with Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) have initiated to form an association in view of growing incidents of forging of share certificates.
Microsoft Corporation on Saturday launched Windows NT (R) Server 4.0, the latest version of the world's best selling sever operating system, in Bangladesh.
